highlights: Moonshot AI released open weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro, an MoE model with 2.8T total and 104B activated parameters.

OpenAI's autonomous pipeline generated patches for 948 local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel, and Anthropic open-sourced FlashProve, a provable inference prototype, under Apache 2.0.

items.title: Moonshot AI releases open weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.summary: Kimi K3.1 Pro is Moonshot AI's open-weight, natively multimodal agentic model, post-trained from Kimi K3. It is an MoE with 2.8T total and 104B activated parameters and a context length of 1048576. In Moonshot's table it scores 65.7 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 51.7 on SWE Marathon v1.1 at max effort. Moonshot recommends vLLM, SGLang or TokenSpeed for serving, so teams with the hardware to self-host can start evaluating it.

evidence.quote: Kimi K3.1 Pro is an open-weight, natively multimodal agentic model, and our most capable 3T-class model to date. Post-trained from Kimi K3 with large-scale joint reinforcement learning across hundreds of downstream domains, it is the first model in the K3.1 series.

items.title: OpenAI pipeline patches 948 Linux kernel privilege-escalation bugs
items.summary: OpenAI built an autonomous pipeline that found, validated and generated patches for 948 local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel. It shows AI handling the full loop from discovery to patch, which teams maintaining low-level code should watch.

items.title: Anthropic open-sources FlashProve for provable LLM inference
items.summary: FlashProve uses zkSNARKs so a model provider can commit to a model and then prove each response was produced by it, without the proof revealing the weights. On Llama 4 Maverick (400B MoE, 4-bit weights), a single H100 generates proofs at around 110 tokens/second, with a ~19 MB proof per 1,024-token request and ~70-95x the GPU time of running the model on vLLM. Code, Lean proofs and documentation are released under Apache 2.0; it is a research prototype, relevant to anyone who wants to verify which model an API actually served.

evidence.quote: Cryptographic proofs of inference solve this problem: they let a model provider commit to a model and then prove that each response was produced by that model.
Claude has produced improvements on zkSNARKs for inference, building a system that is substantially faster than prior open-source systems.

For a large model (Llama 4 Maverick, 400B-parameter mixture of experts), a single H100 GPU generates proofs at around 110 tokens/second, with a proof size of ~19 MB per 1,024-token request, when in 4-bit quantized weights
Importantly, cryptographic techniques ensure that the proof reveals nothing about the model’s weights. Today, we release FlashProve: an open-source performant prototype for provable inference
We release our code, Lean proofs, and documentation under the Apache 2.0 license.
This release is a research prototype
This is ~70-95x the GPU time of running the model itself on vLLM

items.title: Ricursive Intelligence releases dense open-weight Ripple-65B Preview
items.summary: Ripple-65B Preview is a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model behind Ricursive Intelligence's chip design platform: a dense Transformer rather than MoE, pretrained on 12 trillion tokens with up to 1M context. The company reports a U.S. open-weight state-of-the-art 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1. It is available on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud and OpenRouter, and the company says it runs efficiently on local devices such as NVIDIA DGX Spark.

evidence.quote: Today, we release Ripple-65B Preview , a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model that powers our AI chip design platform. The model is pretrained on 12 trillion tokens with support for up to 1M context length.
achieving U.S. open-weight state-of-the-art (80.52) on TerminalBench 2.1
we chose to train a modernized dense Transformer model rather than use Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) like other labs.
The model’s small parameter envelope also enables it to run efficiently on local devices such as NVIDIA DGX Spark
Ripple-65B Preview is available on Hugging Face , Together AI , GMI Cloud , and OpenRouter .

items.title: OpenAI launches Images 2.6
items.summary: Images 2.6 brings faster image generation, GIF creation, more precise editing and new API controls across ChatGPT, Codex and the API. Developers using OpenAI image generation should check the new API controls.

items.title: Deep Principle releases Hydrogen-1.0 open-weight science model
items.summary: Hydrogen-1.0 is post-trained from GLM-5.3 for chemistry, materials science and life sciences; the model is 753B parameters, with BF16 weights under the MIT License. The team reports a 38.3% pass rate on FrontierScience Research versus 33.3% for GPT-6 Astra at max thinking. It is an option for teams that want a self-hosted research assistant, though the numbers come from the team's own evaluation setup.

evidence.quote: Hydrogen-1.0 is a scientific problem-solving and research assistance model developed by Deep Principle based on GLM-5.3.
The Hydrogen-1.0 BF16 model weights in this repository are provided under the MIT License .
Model size 753B params

items.title: Cohere Embed 5 and Rerank 5 arrive on OpenRouter
items.summary: Cohere's Embed 5 and Rerank 5 retrieval models are now available through OpenRouter's single API, with unified billing and no extra SDKs. Embed 5 Pro and Fast share one embedding space, so you can index with Pro and query with Fast, and Rerank 5 scores are calibrated so one relevance threshold works across queries. RAG apps already on OpenRouter can drop a separate vendor integration.

evidence.quote: Embed 5 Pro and Fast share one embedding space. Index with embed-5-pro for quality, then query with embed-5-fast for latency. Rerank 5 scores are calibrated. A score means the same thing across queries and domains, so one relevance threshold can filter out weak context before it reaches the LLM.

items.title: Axion 1.0: an agent foundation model with its full recipe open
items.summary: Axion 1.0 is trained with two lightweight SFT stages followed by reinforcement learning, without dedicated mid-training, DPO or on-policy distillation, and the paper says it is competitive with leading commercial models on several agentic benchmarks. Beyond the weights, the authors release data construction, generation, filtering, verification, prompts and training code; the Axion 1.0-35B reproduction checkpoint on Hugging Face is an MoE with approximately 35B total and 3B active parameters under the Apache License 2.0. Teams that want to reproduce agent post-training can start from it.

evidence.quote: Axion 1.0 achieves strong performance across a broad suite of agentic benchmarks and is competitive with leading commercial models on several of them.
Model Axion 1.0-35B Release Reproduction checkpoint Architecture Mixture of Experts (MoE) Parameters Approximately 35B total, 3B active
This model is released under the Apache License 2.0 .

items.title: LoCo teaches reasoning models when to stop thinking
items.summary: LoCo detects candidate overthinking states in a model's own traces, freezes the reasoning prefix, regenerates shorter verified continuations, and trains on the resulting preference pairs with DPO. Across five math and three code benchmarks it cuts completion length by 41.7%-45.4% on math and 23.4%-36.3% on code while maintaining or improving accuracy. Training data comes entirely from self-generated math traces, which makes it relevant to teams trying to cut reasoning token costs.

items.title: Caper pre-executes coding agent commands before approval
items.summary: Caper pre-executes each shell command a coding agent proposes in a snapshotted sandbox, hands an independent approver a bounded report of the observed effects, commits allowed commands and rolls back blocked ones with a reason the agent can act on. Against six existing systems it has the lowest harmful-outcome rate on SABER (6.7% versus at least 14.8%) and on YoloFS-Ext (7.8% versus at least 35.3%), while blocking 1.0% of the safe twins. It is a useful pattern for anyone building permission controls for coding agents.

items.title: llama.cpp v0.9.0 adds FP8 E4M3 and Mistral Large 4
items.summary: llama.cpp v0.9.0 adds OCP FP8 E4M3 quantization, a flash attn ext rows op that makes the unified KV cache efficient for multi-sequence inference, and support for Clover, Limite, Metis-1.6 and Mistral Large 4. Audio gains Chatterbox TTS and Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, Gemma 4 E2B/E4B get major prefill optimizations, and ggml v0.29.0 brings NCCL-based multi-node tensor parallelism. Local inference users can try FP8 quantization and multi-node setups after upgrading.

items.title: NVIDIA open-sources Auto Ontology, a data context layer for agents
items.summary: Auto Ontology is an NVIDIA Python framework that builds an ontology layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI and API. Natural-language questions are translated to SQL and executed against connected databases, with provenance returned with every answer, under the Apache License 2.0. Teams building enterprise data Q&A or text-to-SQL agents can use it as their context layer.

evidence.quote: NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API.
Natural-language querying of structured data — questions are translated to SQL and executed against connected databases, powered by NVIDIA NIM.
Validate: check generated queries against certified definitions and lineage; return provenance with every answer.
Auto Ontology is distributed under the Apache License 2.0 .

items.title: Collinear AI opens CWE-bench v2 for vulnerability repair
items.summary: CWE-bench v2 opens a public set of 100 tasks covering 91 different CWEs, where an agent gets a real open-source repository and a short instruction to find and fix a weakness. Of the 11 models evaluated, Gemini 4 Argon leads at 67.8% pass@1, just ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 at 67.3%, while DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reaches 57.0% at $0.04 per rollout; even the leader fails 19% of the set on every attempt. The public set, grader and harness are open, so you can evaluate your own security agent.

evidence.quote: In our continued pursuit to push the horizon at Collinear AI , CWE-bench v2 opens up a public set of 100 tasks that anyone can run and evaluate their models on. The setup is the same as before. An agent gets a checkout of a real open-source repository and a short instruction
These 100 tasks cover 91 different CWEs, spanning a wide range of vulnerability classes.
Of the 11 models evaluated, Gemini 4 Argon leads with 67.8% pass@1 and 81.0% pass@4, just ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (67.3% pass@1, 78.0% pass@4).
However, even the leader fails 19% of the set on every attempt, so the long tail is far from solved. The public set, the grader and the harness are open.
DeepSeek reaches 57.0% pass@1 at $0.04 per rollout
On cost, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1017), Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon form the Pareto frontier

items.title: Ai2's StateBench tests state tracking over long documents
items.summary: StateBench uses four difficulty levels to test whether language models can track changing values across long documents. Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna do well on the easier levels but drop to 13% or lower on the longest general finite problems; trained from scratch, Gated DeltaNet and hybrid models generalize almost perfectly on the first three levels while Transformers degrade on longer sequences. Teams building long-context applications or comparing architectures can use it to check state tracking.

evidence.quote: Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna still break down on harder forms of state tracking as inputs grow longer. Four levels of state tracking StateBench consists of four difficulty levels

All four performed well on r-trivial and aperiodic problems. But on soluble and general finite problems, accuracy fell sharply as inputs grew longer, dropping to 13% or lower on the longest general finite problems.

Gated DeltaNet and hybrid models generalized almost perfectly on r-trivial, aperiodic, and soluble problems out to the longest sequences we tested, tens of thousands of assignments. Transformers learned the easier levels but degraded on longer sequences

StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents November 3, 2026 Ai2 Share Tech Report Data Code We’re introducing StateBench , a benchmark for long-context state tracking

items.title: Hugging Face proposes Model Integration Contracts for Transformers
items.summary: A Model Integration Contract pairs a shrunk fixture model with a runnable usage path and human-reviewed baselines, and holds if the usage path on the fixture still produces the baselines; a small UMT5 model on CPU flagged a bug that had stayed in main for almost two months. The tmic CLI drafts the contract, builds the fixture and records baselines locally, with the LLM drafting and a human approving. Authors integrating new models into Transformers can use it to catch regressions cheaply.

evidence.quote: The contract holds if running the usage path on the fixture still produces the baselines.
Nothing crashed, and the bug stayed in main for almost two months. When we later replayed those commits, a small UMT5 model running on CPU flagged it on every one of them.

Our CLI, tmic , creates the contract and builds the fixture. For a new model, an LLM drafts the usage code and manifest, and CPU and GPU runs measure the candidate baselines. The LLM drafts; it doesn't approve.
It drafts the contract, builds the fixture and records its baselines on your machine, asking you to review each step
